Bug_Title: "Object.wait()", "Object.notify()" and "Object.notifyAll()" should only be called from synchronized code
Bug_Details:
The Object.wait(…​) , Object.notify() and Object.notifyAll() methods are used in multithreaded environments
to coordinate interdependent tasks that are performed by different threads. These methods are not thread-safe and by contract, they require the
invoking Thread to own the object’s monitor. If a thread invokes one of these methods without owning the object’s monitor an IllegalMonitorStateException is thrown.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the code by using the Object.wait(…​) method in a non-synchronized context. The bug is triggered when the main thread calls the Object.notifyAll() method, which throws an IllegalMonitorStateException because the main thread does not own the object's monitor.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test case triggered the bug by calling lock.notifyAll() from a non-synchronized context.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that an IllegalMonitorStateException was thrown in the testBug method, which confirms that the bug was triggered. The exception was thrown when the Object.notifyAll() method was called without owning the object's monitor, as required by the bug rule.
